cards.responsibility: Home composition and feature-local UI

cards.responsibility: Research detail UI, media presentation and selectors
expandWhen: Fullscreen or captions require interface and content specialists; geometry requires skeleton guidance.

cards.responsibility: Project showcase and feature-local preview behavior
expandWhen: Asset or workbook changes require content guidance; card geometry requires skeleton guidance.

cards.responsibility: Recommendation cards and selection
expandWhen: Expand to content when source fields change and shared UI when disclosure contracts change.

cards.responsibility: Skill showcase UI
expandWhen: Expand to Home and Projects when shared skill presentation changes.

cards.responsibility: Legal document presentation
expandWhen: Expand to routes and contact security when a policy or trust boundary changes.

cards.responsibility: Resume panel presentation
expandWhen: Expand to content and routes when source or exported fallback behavior changes.

cards.responsibility: Contact form, notifications and browser validation
expandWhen: Endpoint or validation changes require contact-functions and release-security guidance.

cards.responsibility: Route composition, metadata, static fallback and indexing
expandWhen: Expand to the feature and skeleton owners for content or loader changes; test static export without JavaScript.

cards.responsibility: Workbook ingestion, templates, assets and content normalization
expandWhen: Expand to affected features for presentation and release guidance for strict candidate changes.

cards.responsibility: Contact endpoints, shared validation, and server security modules
expandWhen: Migrations, endpoint routes or provider configuration require migrations and release-security guidance.

cards.responsibility: Contact D1 migration history
expandWhen: Expand to contact-functions and release for query compatibility and deployment migration sequencing.

cards.responsibility: Theme preference, transition and palette tokens
expandWhen: Palette, reduced-motion or transition changes require interface guidance and affected shared UI tests.

cards.responsibility: Neutral shared components, shell, and styles
expandWhen: Theme writes, dialogs or feature composition require the relevant theme or feature owner.

cards.responsibility: Shared motion primitives and reduced-motion behavior
expandWhen: Expand to interface guidance for focus or geometry and the consuming feature for its animation.

cards.responsibility: Shared loader routing, alignment, transitions and visual baselines
expandWhen: Any geometry, transition or baseline change requires the skeleton specialist and reviewed Linux baselines.

cards.responsibility: Cross-domain browser and quality test harness
expandWhen: CI assignment changes require CI evidence guidance; loader regressions require the skeleton specialist.

cards.responsibility: Local automation, build adapters and package configuration
expandWhen: Static export changes require routes and release review; CI command changes require CI guidance.

cards.responsibility: Workflow orchestration, candidate snapshots and rerun evidence
expandWhen: Reruns, artifact identity or job dependencies require the CI evidence guide and workflow tests.

cards.responsibility: Release artifacts, deployment and security checks
expandWhen: Changes to endpoints, migrations or infrastructure require those owners and release-security guidance.

cards.responsibility: Terraform ownership, plan policy and branch ruleset
expandWhen: Adoption or cloud mutation requires explicit authorization; coordinate with release and CI owners.

cards.responsibility: Agent navigation and product documentation
expandWhen: Ownership, command or section changes require the affected domain card and registry checks.

commands: npm run test -- src/lib/routing/siteRoutes.test.ts src/app/robots.test.ts src/app/sitemap.test.ts
risks: Static export metadata, route registry, and loading composition must remain aligned.
Static rendering and direct import boundaries are system-wide contracts.
Home ordering and static content selection are shared with route loading footprints.
One detail row stays active per route, and media must retain native no-JavaScript behavior.
Workbook records remain authoritative while local visuals preserve an accessible static fallback.
Recommendation eligibility and private resume boundaries must remain content-safe.
Every hydrated data-theme write uses the transition helper with immediate accessibility fallbacks.
Focus, scroll lock, dismissal, and persistent in-place media behavior share one lifecycle.
Motion always has a reduced-motion and static rendering fallback.
Desktop header and mobile rail expose one canonical route registry with independent controls.
Content is validated at build time and never fetched by browser components.
The static browser flow cannot replace Function-side verification or request enforcement.

commands: npm run test -- functions/api/contact.test.ts functions/api/contact/verify.test.ts scripts/d1Reservation.integration.test.ts
risks: Functions and append-only D1 migrations form an isolated runtime trust boundary.
Focused, browser, and release gates protect different behavior and must remain distinct.
Only the exact verified static artifact is eligible for deployment.
Portable task routing and machine validation must stay synchronized without exposing private paths.
Linux-only zero-difference baselines and all three browser skeleton contracts are mandatory.
Infrastructure configuration, artifact integrity, and observed posture are separate evidence.

The Function route allowlist is public static configuration.
Static response headers are public deployment configuration.
Package scripts and dependencies are repository-root configuration.
The checked-in local configuration template is repository-root documentation.
The Node major-version selector is repository-root configuration.
Browser-test server configuration is repository-root configuration.
